title: Close approximations to the golden mean are rare; poor ones like 2/3 are common

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Close approximations to the golden mean are rare; poor ones like 2/3 are common

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Against the 'ideal angle' theory, phyllotactic arrangements that closely approximate the golden mean (8/13, 13/21, 34/55 and higher) are comparatively rare, while poorer approximations such as 3/5, 2/3 and 1/2 are extremely common.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIV: On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the arrangements by which a better approximation is got, such as 8/13, 13/21, and the very close approximations such as 34/55, 55/89, 89/144, etc., are comparatively rare, while the much less close approximations of 3/5 or 2/3, or even 1/2, are extremely common.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XIV, “On Leaf-Arrangement, or Phyllotaxis”; topic “Divergence angle and the golden mean”. Scope: phyllotaxis across plants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch14-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Frequency categories and outcomes are explicit, and a substantial test can be built from existing images. Resolving the assertion across plants would require a large harmonized survey not currently available as a direct table.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compile divergence fractions or parastichy ratios from a taxonomically stratified plant sample and compare prevalence of the listed close and poor approximations. Higher frequencies of 1/2, 2/3 and 3/5 than 8/13 and above support the claim; opposite frequencies refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Image-based samples overrepresent large, conspicuous reproductive structures.

Ratios are not routinely encoded and require extensive annotation.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.92

operationalizability: 0.96

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Rarity of close golden-mean approximations versus abundance of 1/2, 2/3, and 3/5 is a frequency comparison with a clear alternative, the ideal-angle expectation that better approximations should prevail. The best open count file is sunflowers, where high pairs are common, so it tests the wrong end of the distribution for a flora-wide claim. Broader evidence is real but scattered, and a definitive cross-plant ranking would require a compilation that does not yet exist as a dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Tabulate phyllotactic fractions across leaves, cones, and capitula and compare the frequency of 1/2, 2/3, and 3/5 with that of 8/13, 13/21, and higher Fibonacci approximations. The claim is supported if the coarser fractions dominate the flora; it is refuted if close approximations are the common case outside large capitula.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Sunflowers are enriched for the high pairs the claim says are rare, so that file alone cannot represent phyllotaxis across plants.

Leaf-arrangement surveys remain in botanical compilations rather than one open trait table.
